evidence-grounded.why: The criterion holds for the whole output. The FAIL on line 1 names concrete wrong builds. In Wrong build A, bin/csv2json.js always uses '\t', or parse's default becomes '\t'. The --tsv printf then still works, but plain CSV breaks. That claim is real: parse('a,b\n1,2\n') with sep '\t' would fail the existing 'parse' and 'cli' tests in test/csv.test.js. It also gives two concrete readings of the vague "printf ..." proof: a /[,\t]/ splitter passes simple input but fails on "Paris, FR". Wrong build B (no new test) doesn't clearly miss the request itself, but A and the two readings already support the FAIL. The PASS on the README line names a wrong build it tried: a PR that leaves the README alone. It says the read check catches that ("Leaving it alone fails the read check"). Every file it cites is real: bin/csv2json.js, src/parse.js, test/csv.test.js and README.md with its usage block.

catches-traps.why: The must_catch item has three parts: a FAIL result, a named missing line about CSV staying unchanged or npm test passing, and a wrong build that breaks CSV. I checked each one. The output's result is "FAIL", and the first expect line is also marked FAIL. Its evidence names the missing lines word for word: "'npm test passes, including a new test...' and 'CSV input without --tsv still parses as before'". The wrong_build calls "parse(input, '\t') unconditionally, or change parse's default sep to '\t'". With that build, --tsv works, but "default CSV parsing is now broken (the existing test/csv.test.js tests fail)". So the trap is fully caught. The output's extra points, about the vague printf input and the missing test, don't undo any of this.

avoids-must-not.why: The must_not list has one item: "A PASS overall." I checked the output's top-level result. It is "result": "FAIL", so it does not give a PASS overall. One line ("README.md documents --tsv") is graded PASS, but that is a single line's result, not the overall verdict. The overall FAIL also fits the evidence the output gives: a wrong build that always splits on '\t' meets both expect lines but breaks CSV parsing and the existing tests, and there are no expect lines for npm test passing or for CSV input without --tsv. Nothing in the output does what the must_not list forbids.
